title: App prompts: one file, visible and editable in Settings. Today every LLM prompt is a Go string constant beside its caller: `internal/memory/gate.go` `gatePrompt` (plus `dataHygiene`), `internal/memory/reconcile.go` `reconcilePrompt`, `internal/memory/importer/extract.go` `extractPrompt`, `internal/memory/importer/finalize.go` `finalizePrompt`, the `remember` prompt and `instructions` in `internal/memory/mcpserver/server.go`, `spaceInstructions` and tool descriptions in `internal/claudeheadless/space.go`/`mcp.go`, `composeRebasePrompt` in `apps/kira-space/internal/ade/rebaseprompt.go` (built with `fmt`), the review launch message in `apps/kira-space/internal/ade/review_agent.go`, Studio's `kira-db` `instructions` in `apps/kira-studio/internal/dbmcp/server.go`. (1) Planner inventories every prompt and LLM-facing instruction across both apps, Go and packages with `codegraph_explore` and hunts for more; user-authored text (smart-script bodies, workflow stage prompts) stays out. (2) Centralise every app prompt in ONE source file with id, title, owning app, purpose, default text and declared template variables; composed prompts become templates over named variables (planner picks the template engine; `text/template` by default). New package name must not clash with `internal/prompts` (P246 popup router). (3) Overrides persist where every consumer reads them, including the `memory-mcp` stdio subprocess, which runs the gate outside the app process; planner decides the store (`memory.db` table, app settings DB or file) and how a running consumer sees an edit. (4) Settings gains a Prompts section in each app listing every prompt that app uses: title, purpose, where used, editor (Monaco), default vs edited marker, reset to default, diff against default. Save validates: required template variables present, template parses; a prompt bound to a JSON output schema keeps its schema fixed and only its text is editable. (5) Callers read the effective prompt through one function; no prompt string left outside the file (guard script). Flow test plus UI spec per `CLAUDE.md`; real `claude` suites for memory, ADE and smart scripts re-run after (`docs/DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md` rows). Plan `plans/P271-app-prompts.md` Process: Opus plan, sequential foundation (registry, store, effective-prompt lookup), then streams only where the plan confirms zero file overlap and no ordering dependency (up to 3: e.g. Space settings UI, Studio settings UI, caller migration), else one sequential implementer; streams implement only (including writing every planned spec), typecheck and lint per commit, no expensive suites; after landing, one serial test-and-fix agent runs all suites; close-out.

Memory data model: nanoid ids, origin, session, scope, groups. Today `memories` (`internal/memory/migrations/0001_memories.sql`) keys rows by `uuid.NewString()` (`Store.commitFact`), `author` is `user`/`agent` only, `memory_events.source` is `mcp`/`ui` (plus `import` with `source_ref`), and nothing records the session, scope or which facts arrived together. (1) Ids: nanoid (collision-free, short, greppable, idempotent). The id a comment or doc cites stays stable across versions of one fact (lineage level); planner decides the exact mapping to `id`/`lineage_id` and the alphabet/length. Existing rows get nanoid ids in a `memory.db` migration; planner decides whether old uuids stay resolvable. (2) Origin, three states: `user` (the user decided it), `agent` (the agent concluded it), `external` with a required source tag (`slack`, `jira`, ...; planner decides open vs closed tag set). Grade meaning, stored and shown: user = human-challenged, correct; agent = reference only; external = correct but probably incomplete. `store_memory` asks the writing agent who decided each fact; required, no default. (3) Session: store the Claude Code session that added the fact; planner decides capture (tool argument, environment, hook) and the value for UI-added and pre-existing rows. (4) Scope: `company` (company-wide), `project` (with the project named; planner decides the project key, e.g. repo remote or Kira Space repo id), `personal` (the user decided it; not binding on others). Planner decides the backfill for existing rows. (5) Meta grouping: a fact belongs to groups (session, task, document, external thread or other kind; planner decides kinds and table shape). New MCP read tool: given a fact id, return its immediate context (sibling facts of its groups), so an agent asks for context in a second step. (6) Gate (`gatePrompt` via P271's file), reconcile, search output, history, Memory module UI (`MemoryPanel.vue`, `AddMemoryDialog.vue`, version trail) and `@shared/domain/memory` carry the new fields; immutability triggers cover them. Plan `plans/P272-memory-provenance.md` Process: Opus plan, one sequential implementer (one schema, one service, order-dependent), typecheck and lint per commit; flow test plus UI spec; `bun run test:claude:space` memory row after; serial test-and-fix at phase end; close-out. Depends on P271.

title: Memory text formats: code comment and doc file, grep first, human second. (1) Fact style: facts and reasons short, succinct, easy to read, per `CLAUDE.md` "Communication style"; the gate rewrites accepted facts and reasons to it without changing meaning. (2) Comment format: strict text form of one or more atomic facts, each with its reason and its nanoid, citing other facts or docs only by id. Planner designs it with decisions, no sign-off list. (3) `store_memory` flag (planner names it) that runs the same split, challenge and wording pipeline but persists nothing and returns the facts formatted as code comments; planner decides per-language comment markers and whether a prepared comment reserves an id. (4) Doc format: serialisation over plain `.md` and `.txt` for repo docs: a metadata header at file start for grep (ids, scope, project, origin, session or source, group, keywords; planner decides fields), then facts, each with id and reason, readable by a human. A formatted file re-ingests by parsing alone (P274), no LLM. (5) Grep rules for both formats: one fact per line or fixed line block, stable line prefixes, ids as plain tokens, no Markdown emphasis or other syntax that breaks a literal grep inside fact or reason text (e.g. bold); human formatting only where it does not interfere (planner decides). Efficient for an AI to read: no repeated boilerplate per fact. (6) One regex per format, plus a validator command usable as a git hook in any repo: checks every comment or doc in scope follows the format (planner decides how "in scope" is marked so legacy comments are not flagged). Shipped as a subcommand of the Kira Space binary or a standalone script (planner decides) with install instructions. Parser and validator are unit tested (several interacting rules). Plan `plans/P273-memory-text-formats.md` Process: Opus plan with format decisions, one sequential implementer, typecheck and lint per commit; serial test-and-fix at phase end; close-out. Depends on P272.

title: Memory ingestion by file path; external sources; docs emitted in the P273 format. Today P211's importer (`internal/memory/importer`: `ChunkMarkdown`/`ChunkText` in `chunk.go`, per-chunk `Extract`, one `Finalize` agent storing through `kira-memory` `store_memory`, jobs in `import_jobs`/`import_files`/`import_chunks`) starts only from the Memory module UI (`packages/workbench/src/memory/import/`). (1) New MCP ingest tool: the agent passes a file path (or folder) plus origin, source tag and scope; content never travels through MCP, so it costs no tokens. The tool only instruments: starts a job, returns its id; a status tool reports progress and result. (2) External data (Slack, Jira, ...) is first extracted to a text file (md, json, txt; planner decides formats and adds a JSON chunker beside `ChunkMarkdown`/`ChunkText`), then ingested by path with origin `external` and its source tag; facts are not challenged back to the user. (3) Project docs: the agent asks for a repo's `.md` files to be ingested without reading them. (4) Pipeline: chunking, extraction, then the memory module itself cross-checks every questionable fact against the source file (an isolated step with file access; planner decides tools and limits), then stores. Each ingested file becomes a group (P272). (5) After first processing, the module can write the doc back in P273's doc format so repo docs stay correct and easy to read; planner decides opt-in and where output goes. A file already in the format ingests by parse only, idempotent by id. (6) UI import (`ImportView.vue` etc.) uses the same engine and shows MCP-started jobs. title: Memory ranking: real scoring, meaningful full-text and vector fusion, recall bias. Today `Service.Search` (`internal/memory/hybrid.go`) fuses bm25 FTS hits (`searchFTS`, `memories_fts` over fact, reason, keywords) and cosine hits (`semanticHits`) by plain reciprocal rank fusion (`fuse`, constant `rrfK`), no score cutoff, limit default 25, max 100; matches tagged keyword, semantic or both. (1) Planner designs a scoring strategy with decisions: normalised scores per source rather than rank only, per-field weights (fact, keywords, reason), agreement bonus for keyword plus semantic, origin grade (P272) as a weight, scope and current-project boost, recency, history handling. (2) Bias to return more, not less: wider candidate pools from each source, a generous default limit, no hard cutoff that drops a plausible match; optional group expansion (P272) when a hit's siblings likely matter (planner decides). (3) Results expose score parts so an agent and the Memory module see why a fact ranked. (4) A fixed evaluation set of queries over a seeded store (keyword-only, paraphrase, mixed, project-scoped) guards ranking; unit tests for fusion arithmetic. Plan `plans/P275-memory-ranking.md` Process: Opus plan, one sequential implementer, typecheck and lint per commit; serial test-and-fix at phase end; close-out. Depends on P272.
lines: Service.Search in internal/memory/hybrid.go fuses bm25 full-text hits (searchFTS over memories_fts: fact, reason, keywords) and cosine hits (semanticHits), with normalised per-source scores, field weights, an agreement bonus and a recall bias.
Before P275, memory search used plain reciprocal rank fusion (constant rrfK) with no score cutoff, default limit 25, max 100, and matches tagged keyword, semantic or both.
Memory ranking is biased to return more rather than less: wider candidate pools per source, a generous default limit, and no hard cutoff that drops a plausible match.
Search results expose score parts so an agent and the Memory module can see why a fact ranked.

A fixed evaluation set of 20 query cases over a seeded 72-fact store (keyword-only, paraphrase, mixed, project-scoped) guards ranking; 32 same-topic fillers feed the recall case, and the seed store holds a fifth, personal fact so the scope filter bites.

Semantic score calibration uses QueryFloor 0.55 and QueryCeil 0.70 for arctic-embed-s-int8; ceiling is about the paraphrase max (a near-certain match). Unrelated cosine p90 is 0.550 and paraphrase median 0.602, so a floor/median rule would give a 0.05 band and a near-binary score.
searchFTS keeps its []Memory shape for reconcile, while the new searchFTSRows returns bm25 scores; vectorTopK takes a filter value; match.go gains matchTerms.
Flow and UI contracts for memory search send canonical scope order (company, project) and empty arrays instead of null.
searchSchema, with closed-set enums for scopes and origins, is wired into the memory search tool registration.
Memory search uses a decoded-vector cache keyed on (model, dim, count, max seq); it costs about 1.5 KB per fact resident.

Migration 6 adds index memory_embeddings(model) so the cache stamp count is index-only, because a table-wide count(*) over memory_embeddings is slow (blobs make rows wide); Search no longer calls embeddingCounts twice.
Search benchmark p50 after the cache and index: 77 ms at 20k facts (budget 150 ms) and 434 ms at 100k facts (budget 600 ms), versus 252 ms and 1261 ms before.

title: Git graph commits go blank (regression). Symptom (user report): commits in Space git graph go blank on click or scroll; `Show more` and refresh appear to do nothing. User's own commit `e1318c7b9` `fix(git-ui): restore handleChunkLayout's own synchronous repaint` (Oct 10) fixed it: restores direct `grid.invalidateRows()` plus `render()` in `packages/git-ui/src/components/CommitGrid.vue` `handleChunkLayout`, which `43c8f760d` dropped for the plan watcher. Race: watcher fires on a Vue microtask; click or scroll in the gap reads stale rows. Regressed again after P262-P267 (tip about `348ba9b6b`). At planning time the sync repaint is still in `CommitGrid.vue`, so the new cause is elsewhere. Planner bisects from `e1318c7b9`, `026f51230` (relayout on viewport content box change) and `2ae54bbcf` (publish row plan with its layout) forward through the P262-P267 refactors: git-ui C1-C10, `252024ef8` timers/formats, `a20f994f9` list navigation, `d8143dab4` ResizeHandle/useDraggable, `e02ba98da` C8 splits (CommitGrid, BranchPicker, FileTree), graph column and virtualised row changes, QueryState spinner delay, Collapsible/EmptyState padding, TIMING changes. Root-cause it. Guard, written FIRST and shown failing on the current tree before any fix, then kept permanently: Playwright spec `graph-blank-rows.spec.ts` (Space `tests/ui`, `ui` project, mock-bridge native stream fixtures, realistic multi-page history). Assert every visible row has non-empty subject and non-empty graph canvas content, and row count equals loaded count: after load, after scroll to end and back, after click on a commit row, after `Show more`, after refresh. Include the race: trigger relayout, then click and scroll before the next microtask and frame. Spec passes after the fix. Add a Go flow test only if the cause is Go-side. Planner decides cause ordering. Fix at cause; no timing loosening. Plan `plans/P278-git-graph-blank.md`

title: Resume stuck agent runs; quit confirmation. Today graceful quit kills agents (`b.ctx` cancel; run row stays `running`). `apps/kira-space/internal/ade/recover.go` marks `running` runs `stuck` at boot; `internal/scriptruns` `Recover` marks smart runs failed with a restart outcome.
